summary:
AstraVerd is an interactive tool that helps people investigate trends in Earth data without mistaking a persuasive chart for strong evidence. Users choose a study region, a NASA Earth system variable, and a time period. They can explore the same analysis through a guided Beginner journey or an Advanced workspace with a map, time series, and evidence details.

The project addresses the challenge by making the choices behind a trend visible: where it was measured, which years were included, how the data was processed, and what limits the conclusion. It uses NASA products for air temperature, precipitation, soil moisture, and vegetation greenness. Each result includes its source and method so users can trace it back to the underlying data.

AstraVerd makes Earth science more accessible to students, journalists, and the public while staying honest about uncertainty. Its current trend estimates are descriptive; statistical significance and confidence intervals are not presented as validated results.
details:
AstraVerd is an interactive Earth data investigation tool. Users select a study region on a map, choose an Earth system variable, set a time window, and examine the resulting time series and spatial pattern. They can use a guided Beginner experience or an Advanced workspace with the same underlying data and evidence.

The tool brings together four NASA data products: MERRA-2 air temperature, GPM IMERG precipitation, GLDAS soil moisture, and MODIS vegetation greenness. Its evidence receipt records the dataset, method, coverage, and limitations behind an analysis. A question assistant helps users understand variables and results, while Spin It lets them test how changing the time window can change the story a chart appears to tell.

We built the interface with React, TypeScript, CSS, and Leaflet, supported by a Python API and scientific data processing. English and Arabic interfaces make the investigation accessible to a wider audience.

AstraVerd is designed for students, journalists, and curious members of the public who need to ask better questions of Earth data. The team prioritized traceable sources, clear explanations, and scientific restraint: the current results show descriptive trends, while statistical significance and confidence intervals are withheld until validated.
